note: Built as ballot/lean/mn_endorsements.json is. Each record is one line of one party page, matched to one race and one candidate on the lists already loaded in ballot_local_2026.sqlite (office, place and name all fit, one fit only). Montana has three parties on the 2026 ballot (Republican, Democratic, Libertarian); 'Independent' and 'Non Partisan' are not parties. Under 'endorsements' is only what a page itself calls an endorsement: the Montana Libertarian Party's two state candidates; the Flathead County Republican Central Committee's 'official endorsements' for the June 2 primary (the page was updated on June 9 to mark who advanced); the Missoula County Republican Central Committee's endorsements (two primary pages and its page of November nominees, which says the committee 'endorsed this slate'), which include Dan Wilson for the Supreme Court, an office the ballot prints without a party; and the Gallatin County Republican Central Committee's four primary endorsements. 'stage': 'primary' marks a line from a page about the June 2 primary; 'election' appears only when the candidate is on a primary list and not on the November list. The same endorsement often stands on several pages of one unit: count a candidate once per party. Under 'other_support', with the page's own word in 'kind' and never to be shown as an endorsement: the Montana Republican Party's 'Honor Roll' of 42 legislative candidates in contested primaries (a resolution 'supporting their candidacy in the 2026 Primary Election'; SHA-256 of the PDF 09588090fce018c989764e7740485c1a178123782e91eaa303ab448bc554e7ab); Flathead's 'officially recommended' and 'recommended by the body of the ... Central Committee' for Dan Wilson, and the rest of its November voter guide (a card shown as a picture, read by eye, SHA-256 c3c7204b59a22a8d1d737a4984a3480f79a6b078d49e0b15635664810c091604, the same bytes on both openings); Gallatin's November slate card, which besides the party's own nominees names Dan Wilson and says 'Vote to Retain' of one district judge and two justices of the peace; Lake County's printed voting guide (SHA-256 b962e1b7e90b2f868bab2d0449646275f7884154980fe382693e00745fc14bec), which also names Dan Wilson; the Cascade County Democratic Central Committee's 'official' candidate list, which says 'Any name not on this list is not endorsed by the CCDCC' without saying that those on it are; and the Lewis & Clark County Democratic Central Committee's 'Our Candidates', whose last two lines are candidates for nonpartisan county offices 'supported by us as well'. A line on a partisan office in such a list adds nothing to the party label on the ballot and is kept only so that each list is whole. Lines matched although the page spells the name differently from the ballot keep the page's spelling in 'as_listed' (Zach for Zack Wirth, Anthony for Tony Rosales, Nick for Nicholas Lancette, Charles for Charlie Loveridge, Jed for Jedediah Hinkle, Headly for Headley, Dan for Daniel Hill, May Ann for Mary Ann Dunwell, Mcelyea for McElyea, Bogden Richards for Bogden-Richards). 'JC Windmueller, Montana House' gives no district; he is the only candidate of that name for the House. Missoula's 'Public Service Commission, David Sanders' gives no district; he was on one primary list (District 5) and is not on the November list. Unmatched lines are for counties whose county contests, or whose June primary for county offices, are not loaded, for a legislative seat that is not loaded, or for a seat where the loaded list has no such name; each says which. Federal offices on these pages are outside this file, as are positions on ballot measures and Missoula's 'Do Not Retain' recommendation, which names no judge. Read on 2026-10-02 with the kit's honest User-Agent, each site's robots.txt checked first (none of the party sites forbade it, so nothing is held); every page in 'lists' was opened a second time and a record is kept only if the page still showed it (none was lost). Facebook pages, which are all most county units have, are social media and were not read. One thing for a person to look at: the Montana Republican Party's resolution of August 14, 2026 says the party's nominees in Senate District 9 and House District 24 are barred by term limits and are to be replaced, and a later release speaks of a court's preliminary injunction; the lists loaded here still show the primary winners in those two districts.
